Lipiainen, S., Kuparinen, K., Sermyagina, E., Vakkilainen, E., 2022. Pulp and paper industry in energy transition: Towards energy-efficient and low carbon operation in Finland and Sweden. Sustainable Production and Consumption 29, 421-431. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.spc.2021.10.029

Sector-level energy-transition study (LMDI decomposition, energy efficiency index) for Finland and Sweden 2002-2017; little technology data. Loaded: Table 1 reference electricity and heat consumption for 8 product grades (MWh/t, reprinted from Farla et al. 1997, used as weighting factors); recovery boiler fleet averages for 2017 (capacity tds/d, steam temperature, pressure) for Finland and Sweden; modern recovery boiler steam parameters (100-105 bar, 505 degC, reprinted). NOT loaded: primary energy SEC (primary basis), sector-level per-tonne indicators, CO2 intensities, 2002 fleet values, individual mill gasifier sizes and fuel switches, dry solids contents - all in _other-values.csv; Figs. 1-6 (mill-type energy balances, trends, prices) are charts without printed values; Appendix A production volumes not transcribed (FAO statistics, not technology data). No costs are given. No measures, flows or projections.

1. Table 1 SEC values are 1997 values (Farla et al.) adapted without a stated reference year; authors note they only act as ratios between grades. 2. Table 1 primary energy column is derived (electricity/0.40 + heat/0.80, checks for all grades) but the table does not say so. 3. Steam pressure unit (bar) not stated as gauge or absolute. 4. Fig. 1 mill-type specific energy values are shown only graphically. 5. 'Sebtember' typo in a reference access date; the Finnish 2016 efficiency leap is attributed by the authors to a probable statistical error.
